hook.text: In 2022, Japan spent $60 billion buying yen to stop its free fall. Central banks can fight the market directly.

buildup.text: Intervention means a central bank uses its reserves to buy or sell its own currency on the open market.

discovery.text: It works by overwhelming supply and demand temporarily—a shock that can reverse a trend for days or weeks.

twist.text: Markets are bigger than any central bank. Without policy change backing it, intervention fades and the trend resumes.

climax.text: Intervention is a weapon of last resort. It buys time, not permanent change. Policy must follow through.

punchline.text: You can punch the market, but it punches back.

quiz.question: Why do currency interventions often fail long-term?
options: Without supporting policy changes, market forces eventually resume
Banks run out of reserves instantly
